data.one_liner: Unified overlay popup system for Flutter offering toast, loading, confirm, sheet, menu and more without needing a BuildContext.
data.what_it_does: Provides a single runtime API to show various overlay popups (toast, loading, confirm dialogs, sheets, menus, etc.) on a private overlay above the app. It manages lifecycle, back‑button and route policies centrally, keeping the page route stack clean.
use_when: You need global popups that can be triggered from services or async callbacks
You want a consistent API for different popup types with shared back‑button handling
You prefer not to pass BuildContext around
avoid_when: You need system‑level notifications or push messages
You require platform‑specific UI that isn’t an overlay
You already use a dedicated dialog/sheet library and don’t need a unified system
strengths: No BuildContext required for showing popups
One unified API covers many popup types
Supports toast queuing and custom surfaces
weaknesses: Only works as an in‑app overlay, not for OS notifications
Adds another overlay layer which may conflict with other overlay packages
Learning curve to understand its lifecycle and policies
data.setup_notes: Add unified_popups to pubspec, include Pop.routeObserver in navigatorObservers and use Pop.hostBuilder as the app builder.
